facts: The case involves two appeals arising from a common judgment and order dated February 18, 2003, passed by the High Court of Andhra Pradesh.
One Kota Prasadarao lodged a First Information Report alleging that a dispute had occurred between Karanam Chandraiah and Vanjarapu Savariah in regard to a bund.
15 persons were named in the First Information Report, but 39 persons were put on trial.
The prosecution examined three alleged eye witnesses: PW-1, PW-2, and PW-3.
The learned Sessions Judge and High Court did not place any reliance on the evidence of PW-3.
No charge was framed as against the appellants under Section 302/149 IPC.
All other accused were acquitted of the charges.
Vanjarapu Boddu (accused No. 3) and Duvva Simmayya (accused No. 6) were directed to be acquitted by the High Court.
issues: The delay in filing a special leave petition is condoned.
The court's jurisdiction to alter charges under Section 246 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
The reliability of the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
The sufficiency of the First Information Report as evidence.
The acquittal of accused Nos. 3 and 6 by the High Court.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants submitted that from a perusal of the First Information Report, it would appear that overt acts were alleged also against appellant Nos. 1 and 2 (accused Nos. 1 and 4).
No specific overt act was attributed to any of the appellants in regard to the death of deceased No. 2.

The appellants submitted that although in the First Information Report, the appellant No. 2 (accused No. 4) was alleged to have caused injury to deceased No. 1 but he was acquitted of the said charge and purportedly was convicted only for causing injury to deceased No. 2.
respondent_arguments: The State submitted that failure to frame a charge under Sections 302/149 IPC is not fatal, as the learned trial Judge was entitled to alter the charge in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 46 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
The State submitted that the First Information Report need not contain all the details, but in a case of this nature it is expected that the incident would be narrated in some detail.
court_reasoning: The court observed that the High Court should have considered the matter more closely and dealt with each one of the contentions raised by the appellants.
The court noted that no overt act was attributed to any person in regard to the death of Karanam Chandraiah.
The court held that some bystanders may be falsely implicated, and it is expected that the incident would be narrated in some detail.
holding: Not only no case has been made out to interfere with the judgment of acquittal passed as against the respondents in Criminal Appeal arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 4438/2004 but also the judgment of conviction and sentence passed against the appellants Nos. 3 and 4 in Crl. Appeal No. 784/2004 herein are not sustainable.
The accused Nos. 2 and 6 were acquitted by the High Court, and the court held that they are entitled to be given benefit of doubt as no overt act had been attributed as against them.
